questions.question: The term Blue Line is associated with which of the following games?
questions.questionHtml: The term Blue Line is associated with which of the following games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ice Hockey.

Key Points

  • The term "Blue Line" is a significant part of the game Ice Hockey.
  • It refers to the lines that divide the hockey rink into three zones: the defending zone, neutral zone, and attacking zone.
  • The blue lines play a crucial role in determining offside violations in the game of ice hockey.
  • They are essential in regulating the flow of the game and ensuring that players adhere to the rules related to positioning on the rink.

Additional Information

  • Offside Rule in Ice Hockey
    • The offside rule is one of the fundamental rules in ice hockey, aimed at preventing players from gaining an unfair advantage.
    • A player is considered offside if they enter the attacking zone before the puck crosses the blue line.
    • If an offside violation occurs, the referee stops the play, and a faceoff is conducted in the neutral zone to resume the game.
    • Understanding the offside rule is crucial for players and coaches as it impacts offensive strategies and game planning.
  • Zones on the Rink
    • The ice hockey rink is divided into three zones by two blue lines: the defending zone, the neutral zone, and the attacking zone.
    • The defending zone is the area between the blue line closest to a team's goal and the end boards.
    • The neutral zone lies between the two blue lines, where much of the game's transition play occurs.
    • The attacking zone is the area between the blue line farthest from a team's goal and the end boards, where a team aims to score goals.
  • Importance of the Blue Line
    • The blue lines are critical for maintaining the structure and flow of the game, ensuring that players adhere to the rules of positioning.
    • They are used to judge offside violations and play a role in determining where faceoffs occur on the rink.
    • Blue lines also contribute to the strategic aspects of the game, influencing how teams execute their offensive and defensive plays.
    • Properly understanding and leveraging the blue lines can provide a competitive edge to teams in ice hockey.

questions.question: India first participated in the Olympics in ___________.
questions.questionHtml: India first participated in the Olympics in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1900.

Key Points

  • India's connection to the Olympics dates back to the 1900 Paris Olympics, the second modern Games.
  • Calcutta (now Kolkata)-born Norman Pritchard became the first Indian to take part in an Olympics.
    • He ran in five athletics events - the 60m, the 100m, the 200m, the 110m hurdles and the 200m hurdles.
    • India won its first Olympic medal - a silver in the 200m sprint, as Norman Pritchard crossed the finish line behind Walter Tewksbury of the United States.
    • It made Pritchard the first Asian-born athlete to win an Olympic medal.

  • India first sent its official contingent of athletes at the 1920 Antwerp Olympics.

  • Eminent businessman Dorabji Tata is credited with taking the initiative to form an ‘Indian Olympic Association’ to pick and train athletes who could participate in the 1920 Olympics.

    • The first-ever Indian Olympic contingent comprised Purma Bannerjee (100m and 400m), Phadeppa Chaugule (10000m and marathon), Sadashiv Datar (marathon), Kumar Navale and Randhir Shindes (both wrestling).

Additional Information

  • The Indian Olympic Association was established in the year 1927.
    • It is registered as a Non-Profit Organisation under the Societies Registration Act of 1860.
    • As a member of the IOC and OCA, it is the Indian Olympic Association’s primary mission to develop, promote and protect the Olympic Movement in the country.
  • Olympic Games:
    • The first Olympic games were reportedly staged in Olympia in 776 BCE, marking the Olympics' historical roots in ancient Greece.
    • These ancient games were held every four years in Olympia to honor the Greek god Zeus.
    • The International Olympic Committee (IOC) was founded in 1894, and the first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.
    • Women competed for the first time at the 1900 Games in Paris.
    • Women competed in every sport at the 2012 London Olympics for the first time, thanks to the addition of women's boxing to the Olympic program.
    • The 1940 Olympics are referred to as the "Missing Olympics" since they were moved to Helsinki, Finland, and eventually abandoned due to World War II.
    • The Olympics have been held every four years since 1948.
    • The XXXII Olympics Games were held in Tokyo, Japan.
    • The 2024, 2028 and 2032 Olympic Games are to be held in Paris (France), Los Angeles (USA) and Brisbane (Australia) respectively.

questions.question: After how many Minutes Half Time starts in a Hockey match?

questions.question: The athletes while throwing the discus have to remain inside a circle of how many diameter?
questions.questionHtml: The athletes while throwing the discus have to remain inside a circle of how many diameter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2.5 meters.

Key Points

  •  Discus throw is a track and field event in which the athlete throws a heavy discus as far as possible.
  • The discus throw is one of the oldest Olympic events, dating back to ancient Greece.
  • Essentially, an athlete throws the metal disc by standing inside a 2.5-meter-diameter circle.

Additional Information

  •  The discus has a metallic rim and a circular edge and can be constructed from metal, plastic, fiberglass, or wood. For men, it should have a diameter of 22 cm, and for women, 18 cm.
  • The weight of the discus is fixed at 2kg for the men and 1kg for women. 
  • This circle is known as the throwing circle or the circle of release.

questions.question: In which year was the Board of Control for Cricket in India established
questions.questionHtml: In which year was the Board of Control for Cricket in India established
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1928.

Key Points

  • The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) was set up on December 4, 1928, by a group of players at Delhi's Roshnara Club to end the British monopoly in cricket.
  • The Board of Control for Cricket in India is the governing body for cricket in India.
  • Its headquarters are situated at Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai.

Additional Information

  • The role of the BCCI is to regulate and overlook the growth and development of everything related to Indian Cricket.
  • The cricket board has set rules and regulations in its constitution that behave as guidelines for the National team.
  • BCCI has a lion's share of around 80% of the annual revenue of ICC.

questions.question: What is the duration of a Kabaddi match?
questions.questionHtml: What is the duration of a Kabaddi match?

options.text: Two halves of 40 minutes, with a half time break of 5 minutes
options.html: Two halves of 40 minutes, with a half time break of 5 minutes

options.text: Two halves of 30 minutes, with a half time break of 10 minutes
options.html: Two halves of 30 minutes, with a half time break of 10 minutes

options.text: Two halves of 20 minutes, with a half time break of 5 minutes
options.html: Two halves of 20 minutes, with a half time break of 5 minutes

options.text: Two halves of 45 minutes, with a half time break of 10 minutes
options.html: Two halves of 45 minutes, with a half time break of 10 minutes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Two halves of 20 minutes, with a half time break of 5 minutes.

Key Points

  • A standard Kabaddi match consists of two halves of 20 minutes each.
  • There is a half-time break of 5 minutes between the two halves.
  • The match duration is the same for both men’s and women’s Kabaddi competitions.
  • If the match ends in a tie, extra time can be played to determine the winner.
  • The game is played in 7-player teams with the aim of scoring points by raiding the opponent’s half.

Additional Information

  • Kabaddi:
    • It is a contact team sport that originated in ancient India.
    • The game is popular in South Asia and is the national sport of Bangladesh.
    • It is also played extensively in India, Pakistan, and other Asian countries.
  • Raid:
    • A raid is the action of entering the opponent's half and attempting to touch out as many defensive players as possible.
    • The raider must chant "Kabaddi" continuously during the raid, known as the cant.
  • Defensive Skills:
    • Defenders can use various techniques like chain tackling, blocking, and holding to stop the raider.
    • Successful tackles earn points for the defensive team.
  • Pro Kabaddi League (PKL):
    • A professional Kabaddi league in India that began in 2014.
    • It has significantly increased the popularity of the sport in the country.
    • The league follows a franchise-based model similar to the Indian Premier League (IPL) for cricket.

questions.question: Each game in table tennis consists of how many points?
questions.questionHtml: Each game in table tennis consists of how many points?
questions.solution: In table tennis, each game is played up to 11 points, with a player needing a 2-point margin to win. If both players reach 10 points, the game continues until one achieves a 2-point lead. Matches are typically best-of-five or best-of-seven formats, where the first to win three or four games, respectively, wins the match. This scoring system ensures fairness and competitiveness, similar to other sports like badminton, volleyball, and squash, which also require a 2-point margin to win. These formats promote extended play and excitement in closely contested games.

questions.question: In Volleyball, if the game is tied at ____ in any set (except fifth set), the set continues till one team builds a two-point lead over the other.
questions.questionHtml: In Volleyball, if the game is tied at ____ in any set (except fifth set), the set continues till one team builds a two-point lead over the other.
questions.solution: Volleyball is played between two teams of six players, divided into three front-row and three back-row players, aiming to score by hitting the ball over the net into the opponent's court. If tied at 24-24 (except in the fifth set), play continues until a team leads by two points. Co-ed volleyball involves eight players, with at least three females, while beach volleyball has five players without positional divisions. Water volleyball variants include seven players.

questions.question: If a batsman hits a ball twice other than for the purpose of protecting his wicket or with consent from the opposition then:
questions.questionHtml: If a batsman hits a ball twice other than for the purpose of protecting his wicket or with consent from the opposition then:

options.text: the batsman is given a warning
options.html: the batsman is given a warning

options.text: a bye of five runs is declared
options.html: a bye of five runs is declared

questions.solution: If a batsman hits the ball twice without protecting his wicket or consent from the opposition, he is out. There is no warning or bye given in this case. However, if the batsman intentionally damages the pitch, he will receive a warning. The ball is declared dead when the umpire determines that it is no longer in play. Only the umpire has the authority to make this decision.
